main_text.p: Pelag.cap.2.& oper. post. cont. eundem lib.2.c.CLXXXIV.) Gen. VI,3. Job. XIV, 4. Psal. LI, 7. conf. Ephef. II, 3. (φύσει, i.e. τῇ γενέσει, nativitate) Joh. III, 6. Jef.I, 4. Matth.XVII,17. Philip.II, 15.&c.
Summâ : Duplici nomine Reus judicii & maledictionis seu Condemnationis Dei : Uno,in Adam : altero, in seipso.

Idem tamen,Gratiâ Dei ab æterno Electus: Exod. XXXIII, v.9. Rom. IX, 15. 16. & à Reliquis (λειποῖς[?], Ephef. II, 3.) Vasis iræ, Rom. IX, 22. discretus : 1,Corinth. IV, 7. ut esset Vas misericordiæ: Rom. IX, 23. Secundum propositum illius, qui omnia efficit, pro Voluntatis suæ arbitrio: Ephef. I, 11. Vid. in primis Catena salutis, Rom. VIII, 29. 30. Exempla proftant,Cain & Abel: Genef. IV, 4. 5. Isaac & Ismaël: Genef. XXI, 22. Jacob & Esau, Gen. XXV, 23. Malach.I, 2.3. Rom.IX, 11.–13.
main_text.head: 3. Quæst. An Justitiæ ac Veritati Dei, [Exod. XXIII, 7. Prov. XVII, 15.] sit confentaneum; Deum, [Rom.IV, 5.] justificare impium?
main_text.p: Resp. 1. Veritati DEI confentaneum est: Semen mulieris conterere Caput serpentis: quia, idem gratiosè promisit: Gen.III, v.15. conf. Gen. XII, 3. & XXII, 18. & XXVI, 4. & XXVIII, v.14. cum Gal. III, 8.14. 16.28. & Rom.XVI,20.
2. Justitia DEI non adversatur,Quosdam peccatores servari: quia, illidem, per Mediatorem Jesum Christum plenissimè pro iis est satisfactum.

§. 1. Etenim, cùm Adamus, & in Adamo atque cum Adamo quivis Homo, DEO Creatori suo in omnem filialem obligaretur obedientiam: & verò ille,vix inchoato curriculo,suâ sponte defecisset, lethali veneno peccati hausto, & spiculo mortis, 1, Corinth. XV, 56. (contra quod, thoracem justitiæ originalis indutus, validè munitus erat: Ephef. VI,14. & IV, 24. collat. cum Gen. I, 27. ) ultrò in se admisso; clypeo fidei in DEUM, ejusque Verbum,post tergum rejecto: Gen. III, 4. 5. 6. factus

page.notes: Handwritten "7" in the top right corner is handwriting, not printed, and is left out. Greek in the Pelagius line and "λειποῖς" in the Reliquis parenthesis are read with doubt; the second Greek word of line 2 (γενέσει) is also uncertain. Text ends mid-paragraph ("factus") and continues on the next page. No running head or catchword visible.
